root.label: Mutexes and locks
root.note: A mutex makes critical sections exclusive, and each unlock synchronizes with the next lock.

children.label: Mutex kinds
children.note: All are neither copyable nor movable; their identity is what threads agree on.

children.label: std::mutex
children.note: Plain exclusive mutex with a constexpr constructor, so globals are constant-initialized.

children.label: recursive_mutex
children.note: The owner may relock; unlock as many times; exceeding the unspecified depth throws.

children.label: Timed mutexes
children.note: timed_mutex and recursive_timed_mutex add try_lock_for and try_lock_until.

children.label: Shared mutexes
children.note: shared_mutex (C++17) allows many lock_shared holders or one exclusive owner; no upgrade.

children.label: Spurious try_lock
children.note: try_lock may fail on a free mutex, and a failed try_lock synchronizes with nothing.

children.label: Lock wrappers
children.note: RAII types that tie ownership to a scope, satisfying the Lockable requirements on the inside.

children.label: lock_guard
children.note: Locks in the constructor, unlocks in the destructor; not movable; adopt_lock takes over.

children.label: scoped_lock (C++17)
children.note: Variadic; with several mutexes it uses the std::lock algorithm.

children.label: unique_lock
children.note: Movable, optional ownership, defer_lock and try_to_lock; required by condition_variable.

children.label: shared_lock (C++14)
children.note: Calls lock_shared and unlock_shared, for readers of a shared mutex.

children.label: Unnamed wrappers
children.note: scoped_lock{m}; unlocks at once; unique_lock<mutex>(m); declares a new variable m.

children.label: Deadlock
children.note: A cycle of threads each holding a mutex the next one wants.

children.label: Lock ordering
children.note: A global acquisition order makes cycles impossible.

children.label: std::lock
children.note: Locks several Lockables without deadlock by an unspecified algorithm; unlocks all on exception.

children.label: std::try_lock
children.note: Returns -1 on success, or the zero-based index of the first mutex it could not lock.

children.label: Undefined behavior
children.note: Mutex rules are preconditions, so breaking them is undefined, not an error code.

children.label: Relocking
children.note: Locking a non-recursive mutex the thread already owns; deadlock is common, not guaranteed.

children.label: Foreign unlock
children.note: Only the owning thread may unlock a mutex.

children.label: Owned at death
children.note: Destroying an owned mutex, or a thread ending while it owns one.

children.label: One-time initialization
children.note: Two standard ways to run initialization exactly once under concurrency.

children.label: Magic statics
children.note: Since C++11 concurrent callers wait; a throw means retry; recursive re-entry is undefined.

children.label: call_once
children.note: Exceptional executions leave the flag unset; the returning one synchronizes with passive calls.

children.label: Granularity
children.note: Hold a lock for the shortest stretch that keeps the invariant intact.

children.label: No unknown code
children.note: Callbacks under a lock can relock or invert lock order; snapshot, unlock, then call.

children.label: No leaked references
children.note: A reference to guarded data returned from a locked accessor is unprotected afterwards.
